description: memini operator dashboard — top-to-bottom narrative: live headline health (including the deferred-repair backlog), the write path, recall & retrieval quality, aging & maintenance jobs, embedder & rerank, LLM-backed consolidation/answer, the HTTP surface, and client injection telemetry.

panels.title: Live memories
panels.description: Total live (non-superseded, non-expired) memories across all tiers; a sudden drop means a sweep or dedup pass removed more than expected.

panels.title: Writes /s (5m)
panels.description: Successful Remember writes per second over the last 5m; zero during active agent sessions means writes are failing upstream.

panels.title: Recalls /s (5m)
panels.description: Successful Recall searches per second over the last 5m; the primary read-traffic pulse.

panels.title: HTTP 5xx ratio (15m)
panels.description: Share of HTTP requests answered 5xx over 15m; anything above zero deserves a look, above 5% is an outage.

panels.title: Repair backlog depth
panels.description: Memories currently owing deferred repair (pending + enrich + failed); green is empty, any sustained backlog means writes are storing degraded faster than repairs drain.

panels.title: Repair oldest age
panels.description: Age of the oldest memory still awaiting repair; amber the moment anything waits, red past 1h means the repair loop is stuck or starved.

panels.title: Consolidation queue
panels.description: Depth of the async consolidation queue; a queue that grows without draining delays dedup/supersede decisions.

panels.title: Remember rate by tier
panels.description: Successful Remember writes per second split by tier, plus error/dropped outcomes; red or orange series above zero mean writes are being lost.

panels.title: Degraded (vectorless) writes by reason
panels.description: Writes stored without a vector (keyword-searchable only, queued for deferred repair) because the embedder timed out or errored; any sustained rate means the embedder is unhealthy.

panels.title: Store mutations
panels.description: Raw store write traffic: inserts vs updates (by upsert op), hard deletes from Forget, and tombstones written by consolidation; updates dominating inserts means most writes reinforce existing memories.

panels.title: Forget & supersede outcomes
panels.description: Forget and Supersede API outcomes per second; red error series should stay at zero, orange not_found spikes usually mean a client is retrying stale ids.

panels.title: Content hygiene (sanitizer)
panels.description: Ingestion sanitizer actions: cleaned content was rewritten in place, quarantined (orange) content was judged unsafe to store as-is and needs review if it becomes frequent.

panels.title: Corroboration routing
panels.description: Corroboration attempts on fresh short-term writes (did this confirm something we already know); a rising red error rate means the corroboration path is failing writes silently.

panels.title: Contradiction routing
panels.description: Contradiction attempts on fresh durable writes (did this contradict an existing fact); contradicted events drive supersession, red errors mean conflicts are going undetected.

panels.title: Recall rate by hit-count bucket
panels.description: Successful recalls per second split by how many hits they returned, plus errors; a shift toward the 0-hits bucket means retrieval quality is degrading.

panels.title: Recall degradation (keyword-only fallback)
panels.description: Recalls that fell back to keyword-only search because embedding the query timed out or errored; these return without semantic ranking, so any sustained rate hurts result quality.

panels.title: Recall candidates floored (by tier filter)
panels.description: Candidates dropped from recall responses by the min_rank_score composite floor; a jump means the floor (or a scoring regression) is hiding results users would previously have seen.

panels.title: Recall reinforcement
panels.description: Best-effort reinforcement writes triggered by recall hits (strengthening recalled memories); red errors mean reinforcement is silently failing and ranking will slowly stale.

panels.title: Recall success ratio (15m)
panels.description: Share of Recall calls that completed without error over 15m; below 99% something in the search path is failing.

panels.title: Live memories by tier
panels.description: Live memory count per tier over time; working/episodic should churn while semantic/procedural grow slowly — a cliff in any tier means a sweep or dedup removed too much.

panels.title: Promotion, classification & demotion (per hour)
panels.description: Hourly outcomes of the episodic-to-semantic promotion pass, durable facts it wrote, and omitted-tier writes the marker classifier routed; red promote errors mean durable knowledge is not being distilled. Demotions are the mirror image: stale, never-recalled durable memories retiered down to episodic — a steady demotion stream usually means bulk-imported debris aging out.

panels.title: Decay sweeps & dedup tombstones
panels.description: Memories purged by the decay sweeper (by tier) and tombstoned by the dedup pass, per second; sustained zero forever means aging jobs are not running.

panels.title: Fsck outcomes (per hour)
panels.description: Hourly consistency-sweep outcomes; red errors mean the store's self-check cannot complete and silent corruption may go unnoticed.

panels.title: Repair backlog depth by state
panels.description: Memories owing deferred repair, split by state; red failed entries are permanently vectorless without operator action, and a growing pending line means the repair loop cannot keep up.

panels.title: Repair oldest age by state
panels.description: Age of the oldest memory in each repair state; growth without bound means repairs are queued faster than they drain (the red line marks the 1h alarm threshold).

panels.title: Backfill pending
panels.description: Memories still awaiting embedding backfill and long memories still without chunk vectors; a number that never falls means those memories are unreachable by semantic (or chunked) recall.

panels.title: Repair outcomes by stage
panels.description: Deferred-repair attempt outcomes per second by stage; red parked means a memory gave up retrying and stays vectorless, orange retry churn means the embedder keeps failing under the repair loop.

panels.title: Repair duration p95 by stage
panels.description: 95th-percentile latency of a single deferred repair by stage; climbing durations shrink repair throughput and grow the backlog.

panels.title: Embedder p95 latency by backend
panels.description: 95th-percentile embedder call latency per backend layer; the openai layer reflects the real provider, cached/diskcache should stay near zero.

panels.title: Rerank outcomes by backend
panels.description: Recall rerank attempts per second by backend and result; orange fallback means the reranker failed or timed out and results shipped with pre-rerank ordering.

panels.title: Embedder tokens/s by backend
panels.description: Embedding tokens consumed per second as reported by the API (openai backend only); this is the embed cost driver.

panels.title: Embedder errors by backend
panels.description: Embedder failures per second by backend; any sustained nonzero rate here explains degraded writes and keyword-only recalls elsewhere on this board.

panels.title: Embedder batch size (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Texts per Embed call at the median and 95th percentile; batches stuck at 1 mean the batcher is not coalescing and each write pays a full round trip.

panels.title: In-flight embed & rerank calls
panels.description: Concurrent calls currently held against the embedding and rerank backends; pinned at the concurrency cap means requests are queueing behind the limiter.

panels.title: LLM — consolidation & answer (empty without an LLM configured)
Consolidation outcomes
panels.description: LLM consolidation decisions per second (gated, new, update, supersede, noop); red errors or orange drops mean writes are skipping dedup and duplicates will accumulate.

panels.title: Consolidation queue depth
panels.description: Async consolidation queue depth over time; a sawtooth is normal, monotonic growth means the LLM cannot keep pace with write volume.

panels.title: Dedup effectiveness (15m)
panels.description: Share of consolidated writes that matched an existing memory (update/supersede/noop) rather than creating a new one; a sudden drop to zero suggests the matcher is broken.

panels.title: Answer outcomes
panels.description: Answer API (LLM-synthesized answers over recall) outcomes per second; red errors mean answer requests are burning LLM budget without returning.

panels.title: LLM op latency p95
panels.description: 95th-percentile end-to-end latency of the LLM-backed service ops (answer, promote, dedup, semantic distillation wait); these dominate tail latency when the LLM slows down.

panels.title: HTTP request rate by route & status class
panels.description: Requests per second per route, grouped into status classes; red 5xx traffic is server failure, orange 4xx spikes usually mean a misconfigured client or expired key.

panels.title: HTTP p95 latency by route
panels.description: 95th-percentile HTTP latency per route as clients experience it; compare with the service-op view below to tell transport overhead from service work.

panels.title: Service op latency p95 by op
panels.description: 95th-percentile end-to-end latency of every public service operation (remember, recall, briefing, forget, ...); this is the service-internal view behind the HTTP numbers.

panels.title: HTTP response size (search & briefing, p50 / p90)
panels.description: Response body sizes for the two injection-critical routes; growth here directly inflates the tokens injected into agent context.

panels.title: Injection outcomes by result
panels.description: Client-reported memory injections per second by outcome; suppressed_* series show why memories were withheld (already seen, cooldown, budget, unchanged, score) — a spike in suppressions with flat injections means the hooks are firing but delivering nothing.

panels.title: Injected memories by surface
panels.description: Memories actually injected into model context per second, by hook surface (briefing, prompt, pretool); a silent surface means that hook is broken client-side.

panels.title: Injected tokens per hour by surface
panels.description: Client-side estimate of context tokens injected per hour by surface; this is the direct context-budget cost of memini to the agent.
